concepts_addressed: All Life Paths Have Equal Suffering; Outcome Differs by Choice

claims.text: Greg Short asserts that the feeling of difficulty experienced while pursuing a hard goal is universal — every person working toward something difficult feels exactly the same way. This normalizes struggle as an expected property of ambitious pursuits rather than a personal signal of inadequacy or misalignment.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Applies to any person actively pursuing a goal they describe as hard or difficult
claims.mechanism: If difficulty were idiosyncratic — a personal deficiency — it would vary across people pursuing the same goal. Because it is structural (the goal is hard), every person attempting it encounters equivalent resistance, making the feeling a reliable signal of correct engagement rather than failure.
bounded_by: Does not speak to whether the specific difficulty is productive (stretching capacity) versus a signal to change direction

practices.text: When difficulty arises, reframe it as confirmation that you are working on something genuinely hard — not as evidence you are wrong or uniquely ill-suited for the goal.
Expect difficulty before beginning any ambitious pursuit; treat the absence of discomfort as a warning sign that you are not working at the capacity edge.
